clue.text: One defends a sport I introduced into Georgia

definitions.note: read as 'a thing that defends', a noun phrase

indicators.note: something introduced into a place is set inside it, so one piece goes within the other

explanation.surface: Someone stands up for a sport newly brought into Georgia.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the I is introduced into Georgia; the sport stays outside, in front. 'One defends' reads as a person but means a document that defends.
explanation.definitionFit: An apologia is a formal written justification of one's opinions or conduct, so it is something that defends.

clue.text: Fishy person, say, is linked to church being enthralled by Greek god

indicators.note: to be enthralled by someone is to be held captive by them, so these letters are held inside

blocks.note: the Greek god of shepherds and the wild

explanation.surface: A shady character is connected to a church captivated by an ancient deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fishy' suggests dishonesty, but it points to the star sign of the fishes; 'say' marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A Piscean is born under Pisces, the zodiac sign of the fishes, so such a person is an example of a 'fishy' one.

clue.text: One ranks distance travelled on board

blocks.note: an old measure of distance, about three miles
a board, as in 'bed and board', is a table

explanation.surface: Someone sorts how far people went while they were aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A league table lists teams in order of their results, so it is something that ranks them.

clue.text: Lizard in odd parts of Greece found on floor

indicators.note: the odd parts are the first, third and fifth positions, so only those are kept

blocks.note: to floor someone is to knock them out, KO

explanation.surface: A reptile seen on the ground in scattered corners of Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Floor' looks like the ground the lizard stands on, but it is the verb meaning to knock down.
explanation.definitionFit: A gecko is a small climbing lizard of warm countries.

clue.text: Speaker's prompt in announcing: "Reverse of alchemical process ending in failure"

indicators.note: the ending of the following word is its final letter, which alone is kept

blocks.note: alchemy sought to turn base metal into gold; going backwards is gold (Au) to copper (Cu)

explanation.surface: A newsreader's cue mentions alchemy going wrong and ending in failure.
explanation.walkthrough: Au and Cu are the chemical symbols for gold and copper, so 'gold to copper' is written AU TO CU.
explanation.definitionFit: An Autocue is the screen showing a presenter's script as they talk to camera, a prompting device.

clue.text: Attempt to apprehend popular revolutionary outlaw

indicators.note: to apprehend is to seize and hold, so the first word holds the next inside it
a revolution turns something round, so the word for popular is written backwards

blocks.note: to have a bash is to have an attempt

explanation.surface: Someone tries to arrest a well-liked rebel bandit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outlaw' looks like a noun for the rebel, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To outlaw someone is to exclude them from society, which is to banish them.

clue.text: Regarding certain missiles, function is something spasmodic

blocks.note: a ball is a social function, a dance
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: Of weapons: their working involves a jerky motion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Function' suggests purpose or a maths term; here it is a formal party.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballistic is the adjective for projectiles flying under gravity, as in ballistic missiles.

clue.text: Problem shaking off second horse

indicators.note: to shake something off is to get rid of it, so one letter is dropped

blocks.note: the abbreviation for a second of time

explanation.surface: A difficulty after a runner-up horse throws something off.
explanation.walkthrough: S is taken from the front of SNAG.
explanation.definitionFit: A nag is an old or worn-out horse.

clue.text: Great deal, importing article from France, is deception

indicators.note: something imported is brought inside, so the article goes into the other word

blocks.note: as in 'a sight better', meaning a great deal

explanation.surface: A big trade deal that brings in French goods turns out to be a con.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A sight' is informal English for 'a great deal', as in 'a sight too clever'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight means cunning or trickery, as in sleight of hand.

clue.text: A cute astro gal turned out to provide aid for astronomers

indicators.note: things turned out are tipped over and rearranged, so the letters come out in a new order

explanation.surface: A sweet space-loving girl proves useful to stargazers.
explanation.definitionFit: A star catalogue lists stars with their positions, a reference tool for astronomers.

clue.text: Old pistol recalled a measure of heat

indicators.note: something recalled is called back, so the letters run back the other way

explanation.surface: A vintage handgun has been taken back as a heat gauge.
explanation.walkthrough: Regulo is a British trademark for gas-oven temperature settings, as in 'Regulo 6'.
explanation.definitionFit: Regulo numbers mark the temperature settings on a gas cooker, so each is a measure of heat.

clue.text: Cheat to secure conclusion of decisive game

indicators.note: a word's conclusion is its final letter, the only one kept

blocks.note: to crib is to copy dishonestly
to bag something is to secure it

explanation.surface: Someone cheats to clinch the end of a deciding match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decisive game' reads as one phrase, but 'game' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cribbage is a card game scored with pegs on a board.

clue.text: Commentary on memoir possibly means to improve control

indicators.note: one piece placed on another follows after it, so the commentary is sent second

blocks.note: a bio, or biography, of which a memoir is one kind

explanation.surface: Reviews of an autobiography might help a writer get a grip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' means after here: the commentary follows the memoir.
explanation.definitionFit: Biofeedback uses readings of one's own body signals to learn to regulate them, a technique for gaining control.

clue.text: Meaning to give time over to play guitar or violin?

indicators.note: to give a thing over to something else is to hand its place to it, so one letter is replaced

blocks.note: to strum is to brush the strings casually

explanation.surface: A musician intends to set aside time for practising strings.
explanation.walkthrough: The first T of INTENT is handed over to STRUM, which takes its place.
explanation.definitionFit: Guitar and violin are examples of musical instruments; the question mark flags definition by example.

clue.text: Don't stress about floor covering around piano

indicators.note: one thing set around another surrounds it, so the covering wraps the musical letter

blocks.note: the padding laid beneath a carpet

explanation.surface: Relax about the carpet layers working around the piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't stress' sounds like reassurance, but it means play something down.
explanation.definitionFit: To underplay something is to give it less emphasis than it deserves, so not stressing it.

clue.text: Expression of annoyance contributing to set-to at home

indicators.note: the answer contributes to the following words, being made of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A curse plays a part in a domestic row.
explanation.walkthrough: A set-to is a quarrel; the answer runs from its end through 'at' into 'home'.
explanation.definitionFit: An oath can mean a swear word uttered in anger, an expression of annoyance.

clue.text: Support an alternative for sandwich filling?

blocks.note: a common spread inside a sandwich
as in plan B, the alternative option

explanation.surface: Backing a substitute for what goes in a sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' places the alternative after the filling.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamb is the vertical post at the side of a door or window frame, a structural support.

clue.text: Stop having what music stage often has?

blocks.note: first meaning: give up or call off
second meaning, read as three words: a group of musicians playing on it

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning splits the answer into 'a band on', which is what a concert stage usually has.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon a plan or match is to stop it; split up, the letters describe a band performing on stage.

clue.text: Daughter with competence lacking hint of femininity? That's a shortcoming

indicators.note: lacking something means being without it, so one letter goes missing

explanation.surface: A daughter is capable but not very ladylike: a failing.
explanation.walkthrough: One F is dropped from EFFICIENCY, with D in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A deficiency is a lack or flaw, which is a shortcoming.

clue.text: Fashion, if on the up, encompasses feminine area of influence

indicators.note: in a down entry going up means reading from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards
to encompass is to surround, so the reversed letters wrap round the next one

explanation.surface: Style, if it rises, takes in a womanly domain.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on the up' means read from the bottom, so both words run backwards before the feminine letter goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiefdom was land held under a feudal lord; figuratively it is a sphere where someone holds sway.

clue.text: Red fleece, with edges pinned

indicators.note: something pinned is held fast inside another thing, so these letters sit within it

explanation.surface: A scarlet woolly coat with its borders fastened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleece' looks like the garment or wool, but it is the verb to swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: Crimson is a deep purplish shade of red.

clue.text: Centre of Leeds pedestrianised on the outside without concerns

indicators.note: the centre of a five-letter word is its third letter, the only one kept
something on the outside surrounds what is in the middle

blocks.note: a pedestrianised street is closed to cars

explanation.surface: Leeds city centre has been closed to traffic all around, carefree at last.
explanation.walkthrough: Leeds is a city in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Carefree means free from anxiety or responsibility, which is being without concerns.

clue.text: Fellow getting ahead of family to make a point

definitions.note: read as 'a tool to make a point', a noun

blocks.note: informal British for a person, a bloke

explanation.surface: A man gets in front of his relatives to say something meaningful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make a point' sounds like arguing, but a bodkin is literally pointed.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodkin is a blunt needle or a small pointed tool for piercing holes, so something with which to make a point.

clue.text: Pub against providing joint of beef

blocks.note: a bar is a drinking place

explanation.surface: A pub opposed to serving roast beef.
explanation.definitionFit: A baron of beef is a large roasting cut made of both sirloins joined at the backbone.

clue.text: Bat, in a theatrical way, amused fielder inordinately

indicators.note: inordinately means beyond proper order, so the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A batsman plays theatrically, which hugely entertains a fielder at cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bat' looks like the cricket stroke, but the definition is the German word for the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Die Fledermaus, German for 'the bat', is Johann Strauss's operetta, a bat in stage form.

clue.text: Consume fuel source, releasing power

indicators.note: to release something is to let it go, so that letter leaves

blocks.note: dried bog material burnt for heat

explanation.surface: Burning a power supply lets loose energy.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat is to consume food.

clue.text: Indefinite number — more than required — entering Kentucky is problematic

indicators.note: letters entering a word go inside it

explanation.surface: An uncounted surplus of people pouring into Kentucky causes trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: OTT, short for 'over the top', is British slang for excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A knotty problem is a tangled, hard one to solve, so knotty means problematic.

clue.text: Working well in short dress or more revealing costume

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

explanation.surface: Someone at work looking good in a small frock or something skimpier still.
explanation.definitionFit: A monokini is a topless bathing suit, a swimming costume that shows more than a bikini.
